verses.restored: Kiss [bar—possibly “son” or “in purity”; wording uncertain], lest he be angry and you perish in the way, for his anger may quickly kindle. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

familiar.text: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.

notes.title: Bar in Psalm 2:12
notes.body: The phrase traditionally rendered “Kiss the Son” is unusually difficult. Hebrew/Aramaic bar can be read in more than one way, and ancient/modern witnesses and translators diverge. The restored line leaves the uncertainty visible rather than forcing a single christological reading.

modern.text: Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in your rebellion, when His wrath ignites in an instant. Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.

original.text: נַשְּׁקוּ בַ֡ר פֶּן יֶאֱנַ֤ף וְתֹ֬אבְדוּ דֶ֗רֶךְ כִּֽי יִבְעַ֣ר כִּמְעַ֣ט אַפּ֑וֹ אַ֝שְׁרֵ֗י כָּל ח֥וֹסֵי בֽוֹ

translation_notes: This chapter expands corpus coverage while remaining explicitly pending a deeper Hebrew/source-witness audit. KJV is retained only as the familiar comparison layer.

The completion draft intentionally preserves coherent traditional English syntax where a verse has not yet received a curated Hebrew-sensitive rendering; it does not mix archaic and modern grammar. Major identified lexical/textual issues receive explicit overrides and notes.
safety_note: Ancient royal and conquest poetry is not authorization for theocracy, imperialism, nationalism, collective punishment, or violence against modern nations.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Scrolls where extant, and other relevant witnesses during the global audit.
Preserve Psalm numbering and superscription differences across Hebrew and Greek traditions rather than silently harmonizing them.
